title: Chronobiology: the Circadian Oscillator Network, Entrainment, and Clock-Disruption Disease
author: Young Jae Lee
abstract: The ~24h circadian clock as a self-sustained coupled limit-cycle oscillator network (SCN master + peripheral clocks) on the shared R19 substrate: it free-runs, is entrained by light via a biphasic PRC, synchronises as a master-led network, and gates the HPA setpoint. Disease is clock-environment misalignment; the mind depression seam supplies a contributor mind explicitly locked; chronotherapy is PRC-based timing. A deterministic, DNA-seeded derivation (seed=19), not a toy simulation; efficacy=0.

chapters.title: Grounding: measured DNA emergence, determinism, and falsifiable discriminants
chapters.one_liner: this volume is a deterministic derivation seeded by a measured BMAL1/ARNTL gamma (never fitted), reproducible (seed=19, 2x sha256 identical) across 8 falsifiable discriminants — not a toy simulation

chapters.title: Scope: the circadian clock as a self-sustained oscillator network
chapters.one_liner: the circadian clock is a self-sustained coupled limit-cycle oscillator network on the R19 substrate with a measured BMAL1 gamma; it free-runs and is only entrained by light

chapters.title: Free-running: the molecular clock self-sustains a rhythm with no input
chapters.one_liner: the molecular clock free-runs with zero drive (a regular limit cycle); a strong tonic drive silences it (depolarisation block) — the rhythm lives in a drive window

chapters.title: Entrainment: the phase-response curve and the Arnold tongue
chapters.one_liner: a brief pulse advances or delays the clock by phase (a biphasic light PRC) and a periodic zeitgeber locks it with a range that widens with strength (an Arnold tongue); the PRC bounds re-alignment to ~1 h/day

chapters.title: Master vs network: coupled clocks synchronise, master-led
chapters.one_liner: the body clocks are one coupled network: coherence rises with coupling (a synchronisation transition) and a stronger SCN master pulls peripheral clocks into phase

chapters.title: Setpoint gating: the clock imposes a daily rhythm on the HPA axis
chapters.one_liner: the clock imposes a daily rhythm on the HPA cortisol axis (mind-cited kinetics, no new constant): a gated clock builds a cortisol rhythm an ablated clock lacks

chapters.title: Misalignment: shift work, jet lag, and the dysregulated setpoint
chapters.one_liner: circadian disease is a phase gap not a broken clock: the gated cortisol rhythm peaks at the wrong external time — covering sleep-wake disorders, shift-work cardiometabolic disease, and IARC-2A night-shift cancer

chapters.title: The circadian–mood seam: supplying the contributor mind locked
chapters.one_liner: circadian misalignment flattens the gated HPA cortisol rhythm, supplying the circadian depression contributor mind explicitly locked (withdrawal bias b<0); SIGN only, the felt quality stays in mind

chapters.title: Chronotherapy: re-aligning the clock with the PRC
chapters.one_liner: chronotherapy re-aligns the clock with a PRC-correct zeitgeber while the wrong phase worsens it; four levers off one control law, efficacy=0, not medical advice
